root_idea.summary: The root denotes the opposite of paucity: being numerous, abundant, or increased in quantity or number.
root_idea.development: Its basic quantitative sense extends to comparative superiority, making or acquiring more, rivalry over having more, and intensified abundance such as كَوْثَر.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Form I verb has its own intransitive lexical meaning: becoming numerous or abundant.
The Form II causative is a distinct public verb meaning to make or increase something in quantity.
The Form IV verb has distinct causative and profusive uses.
The Form X verb has distinct desire, usage, and evaluative meanings.
This nominal group is the comparative or superlative adjective/noun أَكْثَر.
كَثِير is a lexical adjective/noun with extensive Quranic usage.
كَثِيرَة is the regular feminine inflection of the same adjective and is represented under كَثِير.
كَثْرَة is a distinct abstract noun meaning abundance or multitude.
كَوْثَر is a distinct intensified noun with Quran-specific interpretations.
تَكَاثُر is a distinct verbal noun denoting competitive accumulation or rivalry in having more.

senses.definition: To become numerous, abundant, or great in quantity; to multiply.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive verb describing an increase or state of plurality in people, things, or quantity.

senses.definition: To make numerous, abundant, or greater in quantity; to increase or multiply something.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative transitive use, with the object being the people, things, or quantity increased.

senses.definition: To make something abundant, numerous, or greater; to multiply it.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative use that may take an explicit object, including an action or state made more extensive.

senses.definition: To do, say, or produce much; to be profuse or excessive in an activity.
senses.usage_conditions: The object may be explicit or suppressed; the construction can describe profuse speech, action, or production.

senses.definition: To desire, seek, or aim to obtain much of something.
senses.usage_conditions: The desired object may be material or immaterial, such as property, good, or another desired quantity.

senses.definition: To do or have much of something; to engage in or produce it abundantly.
senses.usage_conditions: This use is equivalent to doing more or much of an activity or thing, with the relevant object or complement supplied by context.

senses.definition: To reckon or regard something as much, abundant, or great.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive evaluative use concerning the amount or magnitude attributed to the object.

senses.definition: More or most in quantity or number.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative nominal used for relative quantity, numerical majority, or greater abundance; the comparison may be explicit or understood from context.

senses.definition: Many, much, numerous, or abundant; a large quantity or number.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally or substantively with countable and uncountable things, and adverbially for doing something much or extensively. In Quranic usage, abundance can also imply considerable value or benefit, not number alone.

senses.definition: Abundance, multitude, or a large quantity or number.
senses.usage_conditions: An abstract noun describing plentifulness or numerical multitude, including the abundance of a possession or circumstance.

senses.definition: Immense or abundant good, especially the abundant bounty granted to the Prophet.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-specific interpretation of the noun in which intensified abundance denotes great blessing or good rather than a mere numerical quantity.

senses.definition: The river in Paradise associated especially with the Prophet.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-specific referent identified as a paradisiacal river from which other rivers flow.

senses.definition: Rivalry or competitive striving to have more, especially in wealth, status, children, property, or followers.
senses.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or collective construction describing parties competing with one another for superiority in abundance or number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To occur or proceed often from someone or to be done frequently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction describing repeated occurrence of an action or thing, distinct from simply becoming numerous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with another for superiority in number and overcome or surpass them in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal contest between parties, distinct from the collective noun تَكَاثُر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rich or abundant in property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use concerning the abundance of a person's wealth or possessions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm-tree, to produce or put forth its spadix.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To endeavor to acquire much or an abundance of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be knowledge or another desired possession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a vain or false show of abundance or riches, including wealth not actually possessed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or social use involving boastful display or claiming more than one has.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To multiply or increase by degrees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of riches or other things that become more in successive increase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people to multiply against someone and overcome or subdue them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction in which numerical increase results in overpowering another party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dust, to become abundant or greatly increased.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use describing a large, rising quantity of dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The greater, greatest, or main part of a thing; most of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the predominant portion, rather than the general adjective meaning many.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart or pith of a palm-tree, or its spadix.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun, also reported as a variant for the palm spadix.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Frequency or repeated occurrence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage emphasizing how often something occurs rather than only its quantity or number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Richness or wealthiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized extension in which abundance specifically denotes ample property or means.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Companies, troops, or groups of men or animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explicitly restricted in this use to groups of people or animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Often or frequently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adverbial use emphasizing repeated occurrence rather than a large amount or number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much, confused dust rising and diffusing itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or specialized description of turbulent, spreading dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much, used substantively in negative expressions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional substantivized use reported chiefly in negative phrases.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person abounding in good who gives generously or often.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical designation for a generous lord, master, or benefactor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The general lexical noun; the specifically paradisiacal river is separately represented under the Quranic sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pertaining to the greater number of things or cases.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah adjective formed from the comparative notion of the greater number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person possessing wealth, especially much wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial noun describing a wealthy person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or means of making something abundant or multiplying it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An instrumental or causal noun for what produces increase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loquacious, talkative, or a great babbler.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to either a man or a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overcome, overwhelmed, or burdened by the multiplication of others or of claims.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe a person outnumbered and subdued, a place thronged, or someone beset by numerous claimants or seekers of beneficence.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Numerical abundance is Quranic; frequent occurrence is separately classical.
The Form II entry points to the Form IV entry; its causative increase meaning is represented here.
Intransitive profusive use is covered by the Form IV profusive sense.
Becoming rich or abundant in property.
Exclamative abundance of wealth or cattle.
False display of abundance or riches.
People multiplying against and overcoming someone.
Desiring much water is an instance of the same acquisition sense.
Abundance and the distinct frequency use.
Companies or troops of people or animals.
General abundance and specialized dust use.
Large quantities of property or cattle are covered by the general Quranic sense.
A specialized description is reported under كَثِير but the text says the reading probably belongs to كَاثِر.
Paradise river associated with the Prophet.
Nisbah adjective pertaining to the greater number.
A place overwhelmed by a crowd is covered by the same sense.
Being burdened by numerous claims or seekers is covered by the broader overwhelmed sense.

cautions: أَكْثَر appears in separate QAC groups as both the comparative/superlative nominal and a Form IV verb; they are retained as distinct public forms.
كَوْثَر has two Quran-attested interpretive branches in the supplied lexical evidence: abundant good and the river in Paradise.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:kvr:27931:g1:sub4 contains a specialized description under كَثِير, but its editorial note says the correct reading is probably كَاثِر; it is therefore left unresolved rather than assigned to either headword.
